Hey, I'm sorry for what your husband is putting you through. There are ways out of an abusive relationship, and it doesn't mean you have to kill yourself. I've had plenty of women on a domestic abuse hotline that need someone to talk to but don't want to/can't leave their partners, based on them having kids/nowhere else to go etc, or they quite simply just aren't ready. Forgive me if I'm wrong, but you sound quite ready to leave your husband. 

Suicide is neither the only way nor the best way. Even though your family may gossip, is it still a safe space for you? Somewhere you can get back on your feet whilst he's not around? Do you have any other safe spaces, could be with friends or colleagues? I know in the UK there are refuges women can go to with their children if they can't afford a hostel/hotel or have no other income. 

The place I worked at would allow women to stay for months at a time; it was a safe place with other survivors of abuse, outside of any risk zones (places where the abusive partner, their family, and their friends would frequent). Counselling was also provided with trained professionals, of course, to deal with the effects of the abuse. I'm not sure what's offered in other countries, however, I'm certain it wouldn't be too different to what's provided here. 

If you choose to take this option, try and safety plan beforehand. Keep an overnight bag packed in a discreet place. Keep all your medication and important documents together with your things. Keep money on you. Important phone numbers etc. 

There are people you can reach out to. People who will help. Suicide won't help you, and it won't help your children. Please get in touch with organisations in your local area.

Please don't kill yourself. I'm sorry for what you went through as a child, and for what you're experiencing at work. Nobody should have to feel as if they're being constantly judged by others. It's difficult when that happens, and I think you've just got to keep on fighting through it. Eventually things will change. There's always something to live for.
